description: About 16,000 Nigerian nurses migrated to the UK in 2025 alone, taking the five-year total to around 57,000. Peer-reviewed work found about 42,000 nurses left Nigeria in 2022-2024, the largest sub-Saharan African contribution to the NHS nursing workforce in Great Britain.
energy_note: Fifty-seven thousand nurses, in five years, to one country.

description: Between 2021 and 2024, 8,560 Nigerian doctors registered with the UK's General Medical Council - 39% of all international registrations - while another 2,454 went to the US, Canada and Australia. By late 2023, 12,198 Nigerian-trained doctors were licensed in the UK.
energy_note: Thirty-nine per cent of every foreign doctor the UK registered.

aspect: The red list that does not stop it
description: Nigeria is among 54 countries the UK lists as not to be actively recruited from, on WHO criteria - a UHC Service Coverage Index below 50 and health worker density below the global median of 48.6 per 10,000. The code bars active recruitment, not individual applications, which is why the migration continued regardless.
energy_note: Listed as too fragile to recruit from, and recruited from anyway.

aspect: The intention data, which predicts the rest
description: A 2022 study of emigration intentions among skilled health workers found nurses (72%) and doctors (55%) the most likely to migrate. The pipeline is not closing.
energy_note: Seven in ten nurses intending to go.

aspect: The proposed remedy is a bond on a person
description: A push for mandatory five-year national service for doctors before full licensure abroad would solve the outflow by removing the right to leave, which is a different kind of problem.
energy_note: Fixing the exit by closing the door.

aspect: Those who stay carry the gap
description: The nurse who did not leave works the ward the four who left used to staff. Her burnout is the mechanism by which the next four decide.
energy_note: Each departure makes the next one more likely.

aspect: And the training was paid for domestically
description: Nigeria bears the cost of educating the workforce; the destination country receives a trained professional at no training cost. It is a subsidy flowing from a poor health system to rich ones.
money_note: Public cost of training one doctor, transferred abroad.
energy_note: A poor country, subsidising rich countries' hospitals.

description: She is the only doctor on the floor. Four of the six who trained with her are in Britain. She is not angry with them; she has the application half-finished on her own laptop and has had it there for eleven months.
energy_note: Covering for the four who left, with her own form half-typed.
